reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Reduction mammaplasty in a patient whose whole worry is PONV: motion sickness, two prior anesthetics with severe vomiting despite TIVA plus dexamethasone and ondansetron. Plus intraoperative sitting to 80 degrees.

decision.rationale: Fasting is met (Gatorade 0930 for a 1200 case). The deliverable is an aggressive, mechanistically diverse PONV plan and safe beach chair management.

redFlags.evidence: Female, nonsmoker, motion sickness and prior PONV, postop opioids; 2014 admitted for PONV; 2019 failed TIVA plus dexamethasone plus ondansetron.
redFlags.implication: Very high risk; prior prophylaxis failed.
redFlags.action: Multiple different receptor classes: scopolamine patch early, dexamethasone, 5HT3 antagonist, NK1 antagonist (aprepitant), consider amisulpride, haloperidol, or droperidol; propofol TIVA; opioid sparing with Exparel, acetaminophen, NSAID if surgeon agrees; hydration.

redFlags.finding: Sitting 60 to 80 degrees during the case
redFlags.evidence: Surgeon notes: sits patient up for symmetry.
redFlags.implication: Cerebral hypoperfusion if BP is measured at the arm without correction; hypotension.
redFlags.action: Correct BP to brain level, avoid hypotension, secure head and airway during position change.

redFlags.implication: Total local dose and timing with other local anesthetics.
redFlags.action: Coordinate local anesthetic totals; lipid available.
Non paper, gentle tape for eyes and ETT.

planItems.item: Four agent prophylaxis from different classes
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision

boothComplications.why: Emergence in a healthy young patient
